edges.demand: A convex body of affine dimension k holds at most k!·vol + k lattice points.
A gradient of an arithmetic circuit takes constant work per circuit operation.
A basis of a saturated lattice extends to an ambient unimodular basis. Minkowski’s second theorem and Mahler’s basis bound give the basis norm product bounds h, 2h and 9h at ranks one, two and three.
The Moore determinant on F_q-independent entries is nonzero.
A symmetric convex body of volume 2^d·det contains a nonzero lattice point.
The symbolic game and real run agree until two values collide by lazy sampling of the label maps.
A nonzero polynomial of degree ≤d_f vanishes on the valid coin grid with probability ≤d_f/(q−D).
Integer programs in dimension at most four take polynomial time.
Hermite form takes polynomial time with polynomial-size entries.
An interval of length ℓ is searched in O(√ℓ) group operations.

discharge.argument: The stated t_R holds under the same query caps.
The exact target and conditional recovery are stated.
The exact group counts and search bounds under the same hypotheses.

add.label: Direct proof
add.name: Extraction
add.statement: Every extractor output is ⊥ or a witness. In admissible extraction, at u=2Q+2, init and charged first marks cost at most ε_fΣ_s binom(L_s,2) and N_cmp(u)(θ+ε_f)+(binom(L+3u,2)+L+3u)ε_f. A target run has a first mark in {init, guess, charged, good}. For Q_H≤2^λ a guess first mark costs ≤2^λ/N_free. For each b, good first marks with a kernel vector in their row space have probability ≤s_b+2ε_f, with s_b=B_b’s success on uniform Module-SIS. Good first marks with no such vector and no witness output have probability ≤2/q. For adversary time t and ≤Q_H queries per RO, both reductions take at most t+O(Q+d_RQ_H+μ)+poly(D,log q) in the prescribed model. On a witness and honest ciphertext the search target is Λ′=(r(w)−c_w)Ψ^α. For nonzero key weight, the search returning r(w)−c_w, or returning 0 with Ψ^α=0, gives K=[κ]_T. In the extractability experiment Pr[b′=b and Fail]≤1/2+(f_0+f_1)/4. Under (P5), E(2Q+2)≤(Q+1)/2^λ for integer 0≤Q<2^λ. For Appendix A with prescribed points in ℋ and n≤D, let n₁=(2K₁+1)(N+1)+Δ+(ν−1)n_c/J′ and n₂=6K₂(N+1)+3K₂+3n(J+J′)/2+13n−8. The ciphertext has n₁ first-group, 2n₂ second-group and one target element, the seed and μ bits. Encryption computes one generator multiple per element plus one in the target. Outside search decryption uses P=18K₂+4J+2J′+2 pairings, at most (2K₁+1)N first-group additions and MSM total length ≤3n+2D+(ν−1)n_c, at most 12K₂N second-group additions and MSM total length 3n(J+J′)+26n−16, and P−1 target additions and four target scalar multiplications. Search uses O(√|t|+1) group operations when it returns t, and on honest ciphertext O(√g N^{1/4}) in expectation. For binary w with w_0=1 and either prescribed sampler and center, |r(w)−c_w|≤B on the support.
add.proof:
Inverse bound under (I1)–(I6) for the lattice blob's v; write ε=ε_tr, μ=μ_tr.

Trimming. A centered box coordinate has moment generating function M(t)=sinh(gt/2)/(g sinh(t/2)) by summing the progression (limit 1 at zero). Since sinh(x)/x≥1 and (2j+1)!≥6^jj!, M(t)≤exp(g²t²/24). Thus for Y=Bᵀr_I−y_Θ, independence gives E exp(uᵀY)≤exp(uᵀΣ_Θu/2). Put Z=Σ_Θ^{−1/2}Y. Integrating exp(√(99/100) GᵀZ) in both orders with independent standard Gaussian G gives E exp((99/200)‖Z‖²)≤E exp((99/200)‖G‖²)=10^d. Markov and (I2) give lost mass ≤10^d exp(−(99/200)R_tr²)≤ε.

Integral facts. On a largest minor J, Cramer's rule bounds entries of B_iB_J^{−1} by one. Thus J is injective on the span and ‖y‖_∞≤‖y_J‖₁. For saturated Θ, a unimodular extension gives B an integral left inverse, so Bᵀ is onto. For rank-k Δ with k-minors of magnitude <q, a nonzero k-minor survives, making the k nonzero Smith entries in UΔV units mod q. A relation cᵀΔ≡0 mod q makes the first k entries of cᵀU^{−1} multiples of q. Zero them and multiply by U for the integral lift.

Prefixes. Place a largest minor J first. For k≥d factor the first k rows B_k=Y_kC_k, where Y_k bases the saturated prefix span. Its largest minor is J. Since Y_kᵀ is onto, h_k[Z^d:B_kᵀZ^k]=h(Θ). The cyclic enlargement on adding a row has order s_k=h_{k+1}/h_k. A fiber fixes the new coordinate modulo s_k, and each feasible coordinate contributes at most m_k/g because C_k is invertible. Thus m_{k+1}≤m_k⌈g/s_k⌉/g, with m_d=g^{−d}, h_d=1. At s_k≥g every fiber fixes the new coordinate.
For 1<s<g, the ratio is bounded by (1+s/g)/s≤s^{−1+1/b}: if s≥2^b use 1+s/g≤2; otherwise use concavity of s^{1/b}−1−s/2^b, zero at 2^b and nonnegative at 2 since ln(2)/b≥2^{1−b} for b≥7. For s=1 the ceiling factor is one. Hence m^b h^{b−1} is nonincreasing along such steps.
In rank three let r count ratios s_k>1. Their product is h, and telescoping the two products gives ∏(1/s_k+1/g)−1/h≤r(1/2+1/g)^{r−1}/g for r≥1, and zero for r=0. The bound peaks at r=2: the ratio at r=1 exceeds one and for r≥2 it is ≤(3/2)(1/2+1/g)<1. Thus m(Θ)≤g^{−3}ξ_tr(1/h+1/g). For m≥μ this yields h≤H_3 by (I2) and mh≤Γ_3/g³ by (I4).

Image count. For F trimmed by rank-d Θ on I, the map Φ=(Bᵀr_I,r_{i′}) has atoms ≤m(Θ)/g. In the full-dimensional index-q coset case set k=d+1, A=1, δ=q, J empty, B_2=B. Otherwise F^⊥ has rank d′<d, maximal minor J⊆I, and restrictions in span B. Thus B_J has rank d′. Extend a saturated kernel basis of B_J to rebase B=(B_1,B_2) with (B_2)_J=0. Set A=|det(B_1)_J|. The transpose pullback identifies normal spaces by the restriction hypothesis, so k=d+1−d′. For a saturated image normal basis V split rows into V_1 of size d′ and V_2. Pullback on J gives (B_1)_JV_1=Y_JC for a basis Y of F^⊥ and nonsingular integral C. Hence δ=|det V_1| and Aδ≥h(F^⊥). Dropping the first d′ image coordinates is injective on differences since V_1 is invertible. The projected differences lie in the kernel of V_2ᵀ modulo V_1ᵀZ^{d′}, of index δ by transpose surjectivity.
Take k+1 affinely independent projected points; their edge determinant is a nonzero multiple of δ, so vol≥δ/k!. The lattice point bound is then ≤(k+1)!·vol/δ. Its volume is ≤g·vol(Ball_j)(gR_tr/√12)^j√det(B_2ᵀB_2), j=k−1, by the new-coordinate interval and the ellipsoid's singular values. Cauchy–Binet gives A√det(B_2ᵀB_2)≤h(Θ)√binom(N,j), since each product minor is a full B minor by (B_2)_J=0. Multiply by the atom bound and use binom(N,j)≤N^j/j!:
Pr[F]Aδ≤m(Θ)h(Θ)g^j R_tr^j N^{j/2}(j+2)!vol(Ball_j)/√(12^j j!).
The final factor is 2√3, √2π, 20π/(9√2) for j=1,2,3. Apply (I3): in the first case Pr[F]≤Λ_d g^d h(Θ)m(Θ)/q, otherwise Pr[F]h(F^⊥)≤Λ_{d−d′}g^{d−d′}h(Θ)m(Θ).

Regularization by descending rank: a saturated rank-d lattice with m≥μ+(3−d)ε has a regular extension losing ≤(3−d)ε. For d=3 the rank-three bound proves it. For d≤2 choose largest prefix fibers and trim each by R_{k−1} when defined, obtaining F_k of mass ≥m_k−ε≥μ+(2−d)ε. When F_k^⊥ strictly contains the saturated prefix Θ_k, it has rank e>d and e≤3 since Pr[F_k]>g^{−4}. Apply induction to it, obtaining regular R_k of mass ≥m_k−(3−d)ε. If R exists at the final prefix, use it.
Otherwise start at j+1 for the last j with R_j, or at d if none. Beyond that start F_{k+1}^⊥=Θ_{k+1}; s_k≥g would give the new unit normal, which vanishes on J, contradicting injectivity. Hence m_k^b h_k^{b−1} decreases. At d its value is g^{−db}≤μ(Γ_d/g^d)^{b−1} by (I4). At j+1 the second image count applies to R_j of rank e: F_{j+1} has normal Θ_{j+1} with largest minor J and restrictions in span Θ_j⊆span R_j. It gives Pr[F_{j+1}]h_{j+1}≤Λ_{e−d}Γ_e/g^d. By (I4), m_{j+1}≤A_inv Pr[F_{j+1}], and m_{j+1}≤m_j≤Pr[F_j]+ε≤g^{−d−1}+ε≤μP_d^{b−1}. Their product in m_{j+1}(m_{j+1}h_{j+1})^{b−1} gives ≤μ(Γ_d/g^d)^{b−1} since A_invΛ_{e−d}Γ_eP_d≤Γ_d. Finally m≥μ yields regularity.

Support induction. Place the m nonzero coordinates first, omitting coordinate zero. By the lattice blob, θ<p_i=gp(v_{[i]}ᵀ)≤1/g. Maintain a regular saturated Θ, rank d≤3, with v_{[i]} in its reduction, with m(Θ)≥p_i−3ε>μ. At i=1 use Z with h=1, m=1/g and Γ_1≥1 by (I4). At each step h≤H_d by regularity or the rank-three bound.
Minkowski II on the determinant-h projection with ℓ₁ ball volume 2^d/d! gives minima product ≤d!h. Mahler bounds the basis lengths by λ₁,λ₂,3λ₃/2 as present. The coordinate bound lifts this basis with ∏‖B_j‖_∞≤a_d h for a_d=1,2,9. Write v_{[i]}≡Bc′ and c=(c′,v_{i+1}). Trim a maximal modular fiber cᵀΦ=t, obtaining F of mass ≥p_{i+1}−ε>μ. Since v_{i+1}≠0, the image lies in an index-q coset. Full dimension would give Pr[F]≤Λ_dΓ_d/q<μ by (I5) and the image count.
The image difference matrix Δ has rank k≤d. The ellipsoid diameter bounds each moment row by 2R_tr√[(Σ_Θ)_{jj}]≤T_tr‖B_j‖_∞ by Cauchy–Schwarz, and the last row by g−1≤T_tr. Using these bounds (all ≥1 with T_tr for the last row), each k-minor is ≤d!a_dH_dT_tr^d<q in magnitude by (I5). Lift cᵀΔ≡0 integrally and pull back by Φᵀ. The resulting normal reduces to v_{[i+1]}. The normal lattice has rank 1 to 3 by nonzeroness and the fiber bound, and maximum fiber mass ≥Pr[F]>θ−ε≥μ+2ε. Regularize, losing ≤2ε.
Finally Bz_0≡v_{[m]}≠0. The preimage in Z^d of the residue line of z_0 has index q^{d−1}; project it to J for determinant hq^{d−1}. By (I6) and integral h, d!hq^{d−1}≤β^d. The ℓ₁ ball of radius β therefore meets Minkowski's threshold. A nonzero projected point B_Jz lifts to 0<‖Bz‖_∞≤‖B_Jz‖₁≤β<q. Its residue is a nonzero multiple, and zero padding and inverse relabeling give x_0=0.

Deterministic lift for nonzero v with v_0=0, 2β<q and 24β⁴<q³. Omit 0, permute and scale to v_1=1. Four box points of the prefix congruences x_j≡v_jx_1 mod q have four-row minors divisible by q³ by column elimination modulo q and bounded by 24β⁴, so all bounded points span at most three dimensions.
Maintain a bounded basis of the box span S, initially zero. At the next prefix solve integer equations for x∈S×R and x_j−v_jx_1=qz_j with integral slack. For their matrix A take top-first column Hermite form of [A;I]. Nonzero upper blocks have distinct pivots; the others give an integral kernel basis in the lower block by unimodularity. Discard the unique slacks to get a lattice basis of rank ≤4. Bit sizes are polynomial by bounded stored points, elimination and the Hermite bound. In basis coordinates impose box inequalities and test each sign of an integral basis of annihilators of the span found so far, with value ≥1 or ≤−1. Hits increase the span; all failures prove completeness. Each prefix uses O(1) programs in ≤4 variables. At the end return a nonzero box point if present, undoing the permutation and restoring zero. It cannot vanish mod q since β<q. Otherwise return ⊥. Time is polynomial.

Quotients for symmetric W. By the QAP blob, R_W's coset sums are the constraint tests, so R_W is allowed iff they pass. On roots of Z, P_W−Z_0R_W has only Booleanity values at d_j. At ρ it is W_{00}, so subtract W_{00}L_ρ for key division. Conversely either division forces R=R_W on cosets since Z_0≠0 there, and gives the tests by evaluation. Numerator degree ≤2D−2 and divisor degree ≥D−1 give quotient degree <D. Witness wwᵀ passes with W_{00}=1.

Degrees. Put ϖ=Ω_{22}ζζ′ζ″ε, d_f=3D+2n+2K_1+6; ε_f=(d_f+61)/(q−D)<1 gives q−D>d_f. As deg A_i,B_i,L_ρ<D, deg Z_c≤D, deg Z_0=N+2, z has υ-degree <n, k_leg,k_c<n, deg γ_c=k_c+3 and J′Δ′=D−N−2, X_1 exponents have degree ≤d_1=max(D+2K_1,Δ). ϖ clears the single denominators Ω_{22},ζ,ζ′,ζ″,ε of X_2 exponents and α-copies, leaving degree ≤d_2=D+n+7+(J−1)Δ: quotient bases k_c+8+D+(J−1)Δ, remainder bases k_c+N+10+(J′−1)Δ′, H and S k_leg+D+6, cancellation bases 2n+6. So ϖ(val(D)−χκ), with ϖακ of degree D+8, has degree ≤d_1+d_2≤d_f by JΔ≤D+n and Δ≥1, and ϖ-cleared G_1 or G_2 differences ≤max(d_1+5,d_2)≤d_f. On the valid grid (sides ≥q−D, no zero denominator), Schwartz–Zippel bounds nonidentities by ε_f and makes grid identities rational.
At a fixed-r identity put a=Ω_{12}, b=Ω_{22}. Multiply by b, set b=0 and clear the other denominators, independent of a,b. Only H has a pole. Substitute y=B(τ)+t e_j; the t coefficient uses only the two j-poles, whose numerators are α_s s_leg(B_j−y_j) times −a and 1. Hence Σ_{s,leg}α_s s_leg(L_2−aL_1)=0, where L_m is the coefficient-weighted first-group exponent sum against H_m at b=0,y=B(τ).
The first-group types there are 1, ζτ^k, ζ′τ^k, ζ″B_i, π_{k_1}B_i and aπ_{k_1}B_i. Their weighted sums separate by sector α_s and type, with powers of τ independent and B_i independent by B(d_i)=e_i. Without π, s_X υ^{k_leg} distinguishes legs; with π the ε-free terms π s_X υ^{k_c} distinguish cells. Degree two in a kills all F_2,H_1 coefficients. Degree one kills every remaining H_1 coefficient except F_1, matching each F_1,H_1 with its F_2,H_2 coefficient.
In each sector take class π in the multigrading by π, Ω (jointly a,b), ζ, ζ′, ζ″. Matched F,H matrices cancel their hidden bases. The other pairs are F_1 with search bases or G_2 and the three power blocks with the quotient, remainder and cancellation bases. Dividing by α_s, the factor table gives Σ_c γ_c b_c+Φ=χ_sκ, where χ_plain=χ, χ_α=−D_K and
b_c=yᵀ(W_c r−u_c)+yᵀ(W_c−W_cᵀ)A(τ)+(P_{W_c}+h_c Z_c+Z_0 R_c)(τ).
The power blocks give h_c and allowed R_c. Each b_c is independent of ε,υ,s_X; Φ comprises masks, G_2 and cancellation pairs and has no s_X. Coefficients at ε⁰s_X υ^{k_c} give b_key=χ_s L_ρ, all other b_c=0 and then Φ=0. The y-linear part gives W_c r=u_c at d_0 since A(d_0)=0, and A(ρ)=e_0 and A(d_j)=e_j−e_0 make the skew matrix kill a basis. The constant part is the quotient criterion with −h_c,−R_c; evaluation at ρ gives key corner χ_s. In Φ, take the ε-free η_a coefficient: it is πyᵀt_a(υ) plus πP(υ) times the tie-base contribution. Cancel π and compare y_i to get the ties.
Only the H_1 pairs vary with r, so Δr changes a sector by α_sΣ_cγ_c yᵀW_cΔr. Zero stacks thus extend the identity to all r and give χ=0 by the key corner. Conversely an all-r identity makes W_c r=u_c for all r, hence W_c=0. Use differences for formal equality. Pairing a source difference with the opposite generator gives a target expression of the same exponent and zero stacks, so if formally nonzero it is a nonidentity at each fixed r and obeys the coincidence bound.

First marks. Sum the fixed-r ε_f bound over formally distinct received same-group pairs for init. The independent symbolic transcript couples until the first evaluated collision. A good collision then marks a difference (fresh guesses cannot cancel). An earlier target query with a good record marks key, or with no record marks guess. Thus charged requires a bad comparison, and M4 gives target coverage.
Fix that transcript and r. Some nonconstant guess monomial has nonzero scalar or source-group coefficient by the fixed-r bound. After clearing by degree-five ϖ, guess-source, guess-guess and bare-guess degrees are ≤d_f+1,7,6. Independent uniform guesses extend the grid, costing ≤(d_f+1)/(q−D)≤ε_f. Without guesses nonidentities cost ε_f; fixed-r identities of bad target comparisons lie in the selected light stack fiber, of mass ≤θ. That stack is nonzero since zero gives formal equality and χ=0.
At ≤3 new entries per call the guessed pairs and target comparisons total ≤binom(L+3u,2)+L+3u. Without guesses compare a result at call j with ≤L+3j−1 earlier entries, and test the target against ≤Q results plus two inputs. The count ≤QL+3Q(Q+1)/2+2≤N_cmp(u) for u=2Q+2. Sum the bounds.

For guess marks, run with uniform mask and independent key answers, ignoring target hits. Given the exposed injection and coins fixing each query, an unassigned target label is uniform among ≥2^{ℓ_lab}−2−3Q≥N_free strings, since two labels arrive and each call decides at most three. Assigned labels have entries before the mark, so a guess requires hitting the target before assignment. Sum over Q_H queries.

Rank and reduction. Stack rows as M and take a column basis including 0 if nonzero. Fix nonpivot positive coordinates. The fiber prescribes each pivot residue, costing ≤1/g independently at positive pivots and ≤1/g at pivot 0 after conditioning on all positive coordinates. Thus gp(W)≤g^{−d}; heaviness and (P3) give g^{−d}>g^{−4}. Every row-space scalar image maps a largest fiber to one value, so gp(vᵀ)≥gp(W).

Uniform challenge seed blocks give the real law; independent private draws do not affect replies and may be sampled first.
At a good first mark the record invariant gives its expression up to formal equality, from the target record or the result minus the old record. Earlier privately tested target matches were formal equalities or would have marked. Thus a private disagreement detects the good difference if its nonzero cleared polynomial survives, which fails with probability ≤d_f/(q−D)≤ε_f.

Formal representatives agree in stacks and identity at the run's r. By the permitted H_1 pairs, the sector gradient is α_sΣ_{c,i}γ_c y_i W^s_{c,i}, with W^s_{c,i} the cell row i. An alpha mark has zero plain gradient. A nonzero functional on the row space yields after dividing by α_sπ a nonzero polynomial of degree ≤n+2: γ_c/π=s_X υ^{k_c}(1+εω^{2k_1}), and the ε-free monomials s_X υ^{k_c}y_i are distinct. For each fresh gradient choose a functional killing the prior span if proper. The chance of failing to extend is ≤(n+2)/(q−D), so three draws span except with probability ≤3(n+2)/(q−D)≤ε_f.
With detection and spanning, the sector order obtains a kernel vector v in the mark space if no earlier solution was found. Since z(v)=0, v_0=0, and gp(vᵀ)≥gp(W)>θ. Conditions (P3),(P4) give a short lift. Any such kernel lift has x_0≡0 and |x_0|≤β<q, so x_0=0. Packing its remaining coefficients with zero padding gives positive norm ≤β and zero challenge image by the forms identity. The two private error bounds give s_b+2ε_f.

Witness existence for a nonzero usable rank-d stack, d≤3, without a kernel vector. Let U have a row-space basis as columns, u_j its transposed rows, and h_s=Uᵀσ^s(z) over K=F_{q^n}. The entries of h_0, hence h_a, are F_q-independent, where (a,b,c)=(n/2−1,n/2,n/2+1). Moore's determinant makes the first d consecutive conjugates independent, so h_a,h_b,h_c span K^d.
The U-weight, V-weight and conjugated U-weight assemblies are UM_sUᵀ for s=a,b,c, with symmetric M_s by a left inverse of U on both sides. The ties give M_s h_t=M_t h_s. Testing against spanning h_t makes every relation among h_s hold among M_s, so M_s=M(h_s) for a linear M. The ties and matrix symmetry make T(h,u,v)=uᵀM(h)v symmetric. Booleanity gives T(h,u_j,u_j−u_0)=0 for all h by spanning. Conjugacy gives M_a=σ^a(M_c), M_b=σ^b(M_b), since a+c=n and the V assembly is even.
If u_0=0, in a basis from the other rows T vanishes on repeats. Only d=3 allows a nonzero coefficient t on distinct indices. Each off-diagonal entry of M_s is t times the complementary coordinate of h_s. The two conjugacies imply t h_a=σ^a(t)h_0 and t h_b=σ^b(t)h_0. Thus t≠0 contradicts spanning, and T=0 contradicts the nonzero stack since coefficients of the U and V assemblies encode its cells.
Otherwise extend u_0 to a row basis. For binary δ of length d−1 take p_δ with coordinate pairings (1,δ) in that basis. Set w_δ=Up_δ and z_δ=z(w_δ)≠0. Basis triples reduce by Booleanity to subsets A of nonzero indices, replacing repeats by index zero. The cubes of pairing with p_δ are 1_{A⊆supp δ} on these triples, triangular with ones on the diagonal. They span T. Pairs also realize every A since d−1≤2, so the squares p_δp_δᵀ are independent. Thus M_s=Σ_δ c_δ σ^s(z_δ)p_δp_δᵀ. By square independence both conjugacies fix c_δ/z_δ under σ^a and σ^b, hence under σ. Write χ_δ=c_δ/z_δ∈F_q.
For each base-field passage test L, the assemblies pass by cellwise passage, linearity and conjugation. Therefore h_0ᵀQh_s=0 with Q=Σ_δ χ_δ L(w_δw_δᵀ)p_δp_δᵀ over F_q. Spanning and F_q-independence give Q=0. By square independence any δ with χ_δ≠0 passes every test. Such a δ exists by nonzeroness, and w_δ has corner one, hence is a witness.

Outputs are checked witnesses. A good difference uses the tested difference by the record invariant. A good key record comes from a tested result, since received target stacks are zero and guesses have variables. Formal equality preserves sketches, so the mark sketches are tested unless already successful.
By symmetry (v_c)_c↦Σ_cW_cv_c surjects onto the row space. Its three independent uniform probes give a coordinate matrix with d≤3 independent uniform rows in F_q³, independently of the marked run. Sequential row tests give rank loss probability ≤Σ_{j<d}q^{j−3}<2/q. At full rank the tested span contains the witness just proved. It has entry 1 at coordinate 0, so 0 is a pivot, and Boolean entries; it is a candidate.

Timing. Track both label maps and rejections. With U undecided strings and V unused exponents, a uniform remaining injection validates an undecided operand with probability V/U. Draw uniformly from [1,U]: at ≤V assign a uniform unused exponent, else record rejection. For unassigned result exponents draw uniformly from undecided strings. The assigned generator keeps U in range. Each of ≤2 operand decisions, one result, the eligibility flag and negation lookup for names, and circuit or private evaluation use O(1) primitive work; missing records start at zero.
Memoize oracle answers: after installing the seed challenge, each miss needs d_R field draws or one key-set draw, for O(d_RQ_H). Assign κ's label without a record and memoize its key answer. Masking and advice cost O(μ). The O(DN) QAP coefficient advice and published formulas give polynomial evaluation and input differentiation at the fixed points by N,n≤D, JΔ≤D+n, J′Δ′≤D (J′=1 if empty), k d_R<n. Six reverse passes per candidate (≤2) cost O(Q) plus the input work. Zero the other sector's second pairing inputs; direct target terms have zero r-derivative. Kernel intersection, lift and packing are polynomial. Add t.

For Comb, W_c=ξ_cwwᵀ kills skew and yields r(w)ψ for ψ=y(w)Σ_cγ_cξ_c. Chunk pairings subtract the witness quotients and remainders, leaving ξ_keyκ. Honest ties are w times the numerators of x_a^0, so divisibility and w_0=1 justify those divisions; the mask identity and coefficient ranges cancel the mask. Thus Λ=[ξ_keyκ+r(w)ψ]_T, and first left coordinates paired with leg scalars give Ψ=[ψ]_T. Second-input scaling gives Λ^α=αΛ and Ψ^α=αΨ, so Λ′=(r(w)−c_w)Ψ^α. At nonzero weight the correct search t cancels the search term in K; if Ψ^α=0 then Ψ=0 since α≠0, so t=0 suffices. Both give K=[κ]_T.

In the common mask run the target event and off-target output are independent of b. Put p=Pr[Tgt], f=(f_0+f_1)/2≤p. Success with failure is ≤(1−p)/2+f≤1/2+f/2.
The quadratic coefficient (θ+10ε_f)/2 makes E convex. By (P5) its endpoint values at 2,2^{λ+1} are bounded by u/2^{λ+1}, hence so are all intermediate values. Set u=2Q+2.

Efficiency. The four left block sizes (F, quotient, remainder, Y) are 2K₁(N+1), Δ, (ν−1)n_c/J′, N+1.
